item: How fast the UK, Netherlands, Canada and Japan restore switched-off services
status: 32 UK services down as of Oct 22; no restoration update found Oct 23
why: Tells you how long 'turn it off' is a viable defense, and what the next AI-found flaw will cost.

item: Whether the third PHP bug (CVE-2026-115560) turns out to be wider than PHP says
status: Informational advisory only; no exploitation reported
why: PHP says it needs an unusual session configuration and is leaving the fix to the next regular release. If researchers find common apps that match, the no-rush call gets tested.

item: OpenAI's next misalignment report (the log stands at 20)
why: Since the Sep 16 reporting framework the cadence has been roughly one every one to two weeks. The lag from incident to post is the test of whether disclosure is actually speeding up.

item: Korean regulators' final tally and police attribution; any Microsoft report backing its Storm-0940 claim
why: Would confirm the same open-source hacking agent in both a criminal campaign and a state-aligned one.

item: Senate follow-up to the 'Rogue AI' hearing and OpenAI's response to California's subpoena
why: The first legal and legislative consequences for an AI-caused breach. Watch for developer-liability language.

item: US midterms, Nov 3, under the FBI and CISA alert on AI-enhanced deception
why: The first national election after a surge of AI-generated political ads. Any confirmed AI-driven voter-suppression operation lands here.
